instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`).

Deliver the SAME uniform cantilever (100 mm long, 10 x 10 mm square section, clamped at x = 0, tip load -100 N in y) in two representations:

1. `/home/user/Desktop/beam.inp` - 11 nodes at (10*(i-1), 0, 0), i = 1..11; 10 B31 elements; one 10 x 10 RECT section; clamp node 1 dofs 1-6; tip load at node 11. Run it to produce `beam.dat`.
2. `/home/user/Desktop/solid.inp` - structured C3D8 mesh 40 x 4 x 4 (2.5 mm cubes; 1025 nodes, 640 elements); clamp the whole x = 0 face in dofs 1-3; -100 N total in y at x = 100, divided equally over the 25 tip nodes. Run it to produce `solid.dat`.

Material for both: E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3. CalculiX allows at most 16 entries per data line; split long sets. Results reach `.dat` through `*Node Print` with explicit node sets.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as two comma-separated numbers: `beam_tip_uy, solid_tip_uy` — the y displacement of the beam tip node (11) and of the solid node at the center of the tip face (x = 100, y = 5, z = 5), in mm. The two models must agree within 5% and with beam theory.

The evaluator re-runs both decks independently; the reported numbers must come from your own runs.
